cards.text: Psalm 148 opens with one word: "Hallelujah!" Then the psalm writer starts calling out, one after another, who should praise the LORD. Friend, this man has a LIST, and he calls it out like the front desk at the busiest office in the world.

cards.question: Every list has to start somewhere. Where does the psalm writer first call for praise to come from?
Up in the heavens, the first ones the psalm writer calls on to praise the LORD are all His ___.

cards.text: After the angels and all His heavenly hosts, he calls out to the lights in the sky: "Praise Him, O sun and moon; praise Him, all you shining stars." Friend, that's the whole lighting crew of the sky getting called up, and here I am with an oven light that only comes on if you SMACK the door.

cards.question: After the sun, moon and stars, the psalm writer is done with the sky. Nothing higher gets called on to praise the LORD.

cards.text: He goes even higher: "Praise Him, O highest heavens, and you waters above the skies." This man is checking the TOP shelf, friend, the one even I can't reach, and I've got a gold base AND a tall hat.

cards.question: Everything up in the heavens is called to praise the name of the LORD. What reason does the psalm writer give?

answers.text: He commanded and they were created
They were made to serve people
They live closest to His throne

cards.question: After creating everything up in the heavens, God issued a decree. The psalm writer says that decree will never pass away.

cards.text: He established everything up there forever and ever. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer next to an expired coupon that still believed in itself, so NEVER running out sounds pretty amazing to me.

cards.question: The heavens are covered, from the angels all the way up to the highest heavens. Now the psalm writer calls for praise to come from ___.

cards.text: Down on the earth, he starts with all great sea creatures and ocean depths. Friend, people's emails land in spam from across the hall, and the bottom of the OCEAN makes this list first.

cards.question: Next on the earth's list is the weather. What does the psalm writer say the powerful wind is doing?

cards.text: Lightning and hail, snow and clouds, the whole forecast gets called on, friend. A phone sees that lineup and sends ELEVEN alerts, but the psalm writer sees it and hands it a HYMNAL.

cards.question: Still on the earth, the psalm writer calls on trees to praise the LORD too.

cards.text: Mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars, wild animals and all cattle, crawling creatures and flying birds. Friend, that's every hill, tree and critter in one line, and back in the Millers' kitchen I couldn't get six little cookie cutters to line up for ONE batch.

cards.question: After the animals, the psalm writer finally gets to people. Who's at the top of that list?

answers.text: Kings and rulers of the earth

cards.text: Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all rulers of the earth. The folks who run the world get called right after the crawling creatures and the birds, friend, so NO crown gets you a better seat in THIS choir.

cards.question: When the psalm writer calls on people to praise the LORD, he calls the old and the young separately, one group at a time.

cards.text: Young men and maidens, old and young together. Grandpa and the grandkid singing the same song, friend, that's a duet I'd buy a ticket to, and I don't even have a WALLET.

cards.question: Now everything on the earth gets the call: "Let them praise the name of the LORD…" What reason does the psalm writer give?

answers.text: His throne rests on the earth
His mercy fills the whole earth

cards.text: His splendor is above the earth and the heavens, and then the psalm turns to His people: He has raised up a horn for them, the praise of all His saints. Friend, it's like the camera at a packed stadium panning the WHOLE crowd and then zooming right in on one row.

cards.question: At the very end, the psalm writer names His people: Israel. How does he describe them?

answers.text: A people sent to the nations

cards.text: And the psalm ends right where it started: "Hallelujah!" He opened with it and closed with it, friend, with all of heaven and earth packed in between like a cookie box filled RIGHT up to the lid.
